questions.question: The rank of matrix \( \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & 4 & 2 & 5 \\ 5 & 6 & 2 & 7 \\ 7 & 8 & 2 & 9 \end{bmatrix} \) is
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: A \(4 \times 4\) matrix:\[A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & 4 & 2 & 5 \\ 5 & 6 & 2 & 7 \\ 7 & 8 & 2 & 9 \end{bmatrix} \]
  • Aim: Determine the rank of the matrix.

3. Core Concepts:

Rank of a Matrix: The number of linearly independent rows or columns in a matrix.

Gaussian Elimination: Converting the matrix into row echelon form using elementary row operations. The rank equals the number of non-zero rows in this form.

4. Solution Method:

Apply elementary row operations to eliminate non-zero elements below the main diagonal, then count the non-zero rows.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Initial matrix:\[A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & 4 & 2 & 5 \\ 5 & 6 & 2 & 7 \\ 7 & 8 & 2 & 9 \end{bmatrix} \]
  2. Step 2: Eliminate entries below pivot in column 1.
    \(R_2 \leftarrow R_2 - 3R_1\),   \(R_3 \leftarrow R_3 - 5R_1\),   \(R_4 \leftarrow R_4 - 7R_1\)\[\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 & -4 \\ 0 & -4 & -8 & -8 \\ 0 & -6 & -12 & -12 \end{bmatrix} \]
  3. Step 3: Eliminate entries below pivot in column 2.
    Observe \(R_3 = 2R_2\) and \(R_4 = 3R_2\).
    \(R_3 \leftarrow R_3 - 2R_2\),   \(R_4 \leftarrow R_4 - 3R_2\)\[\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \]
  4. Step 4: Count non-zero rows → 2 non-zero rows.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 2  |  Correct option: (B)

questions.question: If \( P = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix} \) and \( Q = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \) then \( Q^T P^T \) is
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: \(P = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(Q = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\)
  • Aim: Find the value of \(Q^T P^T\).

3. Core Concepts:

Matrix Transpose (\(A^T\)): Replaces rows with columns.

Reversal Law of Transpose: \((PQ)^T = Q^T P^T\)

4. Solution Method:

Compute transposes \(Q^T\) and \(P^T\) directly, then multiply \(Q^T P^T\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Find transposes\[P^T = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ 2 & 4 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad Q^T = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \](Note: \(Q\) is symmetric, so \(Q^T = Q\))
  2. Step 2: Multiply \(Q^T P^T\)\[Q^T P^T = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ 2 & 4 \end{bmatrix} \]
    ElementCalculationValue
    (1,1)\(0\times1 + 1\times2\)2
    (1,2)\(0\times3 + 1\times4\)4
    (2,1)\(1\times1 + 0\times2\)1
    (2,2)\(1\times3 + 0\times4\)3
    \[Q^T P^T = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 4 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 4 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\)  |  Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | GA Q3
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: The shape of the cumulative distribution function of Gaussian distribution is
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Probability and Statistics

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data: A standard continuous Gaussian (Normal) probability distribution.
  • Aim: Identify the visual shape of its Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF).

3. Core Concepts:

Probability Density Function (PDF): The Gaussian PDF \(f(x)\) produces the symmetric bell-shaped curve.

Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF):\[F(x) = \int_{-\infty}^{x} f(t)\, dt \]The CDF gives the probability that a random variable \(X \leq x\). It monotonically increases from 0 (at \(-\infty\)) to 1 (at \(+\infty\)).

4. Solution Method:

By integrating the symmetric bell curve, the accumulation starts slowly, accelerates at the mean (point of inflection), and plateaus as it approaches 1 — producing a classical sigmoid curve.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  • At \(x \to -\infty\): \(F(x) \to 0\)
  • At \(x = \mu\) (mean): \(F(x) = 0.5\) — slope is maximum (point of inflection)
  • At \(x \to +\infty\): \(F(x) \to 1\)

Connecting these behavioral bounds results in an S-shaped (sigmoid) curve.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: S-shaped curve  |  Correct option: (D)

questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
A propped cantilever beam EF is subjected to a unit moving load as shown in the figure (not to scale). The sign convention for positive shear force at the left and right sides of any section is also shown.



The CORRECT qualitative nature of the influence line diagram for shear force at G is
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Influence Line Diagrams

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Propped cantilever beam EF (Fixed at E, Roller at F)
    • Intermediate section G
    • Sign convention: positive shear → left part moves DOWN, right part moves UP
  • Aim: Determine the correct qualitative nature of the ILD for shear force at G.

3. Core Concepts:

Müller-Breslau Principle: The ILD for any stress function takes the shape of the deflected curve when a unit displacement corresponding to that function is introduced.

Indeterminacy: A propped cantilever has static indeterminacy of 1. The deflected shape must consist of curved lines, not straight lines.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Rule out ILD shapes with straight lines (eliminates options with piecewise linear diagrams).
  2. Introduce a positive shear release at G.
  3. Enforce boundary conditions at E (fixed) and F (roller) to trace the elastic curve.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Since the beam is indeterminate, the ILD must be formed by curved lines — this immediately eliminates options with straight lines.
  2. Step 2: Apply positive shear release: force the left side of G downward (negative domain) and the right side of G upward (positive domain).
  3. Step 3: Trace deflections with boundary constraints:
    • Segment E → G: Fixed support at E → zero deflection and zero slope at E. The curve starts horizontal at E and arcs downward to the left of G (negative ordinates).
    • Segment G → F: Right side of G is forced upward. Roller at F → zero displacement but non-zero slope. Curve arcs from positive at G down to zero at F.
    This behavior matches the option showing zero slope at E, negative curved region from E to G, and positive curved region from G to F.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Curved ILD — negative ordinates left of G, positive ordinates right of G, zero slope at fixed end E  |  Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | GA Q5
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Limit State Design of Beams & Slabs
questions.question: Gypsum is typically added in cement to
questions.explanation:
Building Materials | Concrete Technology

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data: Gypsum added to cement.
  • Aim: Identify the primary chemical purpose of this addition.

3. Core Concepts:

Bogue's Compounds: Cement clinker contains \(C_3A\) (Tricalcium aluminate), which reacts violently and rapidly with water.

Flash Set: Premature stiffening caused by rapid hydration of \(C_3A\) with immense heat evolution.

Retardation by Gypsum: Gypsum (\(CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O\)) is interground with clinker (~3–5%). It reacts with \(C_3A\) to form an insoluble coating of ettringite (calcium sulphoaluminate) over cement grains, temporarily delaying further hydration and preventing flash/quick setting.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  • Option (B) "enhance hardening": Incorrect — \(C_3S\) and \(C_2S\) dictate hardening/strength.
  • Option (C) "increase workability": Incorrect — plasticizers and admixtures control this.
  • Option (D) "decrease heat of hydration": Incorrect — low \(C_3A\) and \(C_3S\) proportions achieve this.
  • Option (A) "prevent quick setting": Correct — gypsum retards \(C_3A\)'s violent reaction, preventing flash/quick setting.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Prevent quick setting  |  Correct option: (A)

questions.question: The direct and indirect costs estimated by a contractor for bidding a project is ₹160000 and ₹20000 respectively. If the mark up applied is 10% of the bid price, the quoted price (in ₹) of the contractor is
questions.explanation:
Construction Planning & Management | Cost Estimation

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Direct Cost (\(DC\)) = ₹1,60,000
    • Indirect Cost (\(IC\)) = ₹20,000
    • Markup = 10% of the bid price
  • Aim: Calculate the quoted bid price.

3. Core Concepts:

Total Estimated Cost (\(TC\)): Sum of direct and indirect costs.

Bid Price (\(B\)):\[B = TC + \text{Markup} \]Since markup is expressed as a percentage of the bid price (not cost), \(B\) appears on both sides of the equation.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate total cost \(TC = DC + IC\).
  2. Express markup as \(0.10 \times B\) and form an algebraic equation.
  3. Solve for \(B\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Total Cost\[TC = 1{,}60{,}000 + 20{,}000 = 1{,}80{,}000 \text{ ₹} \]
  2. Step 2: Bid Price Equation\[B = TC + 0.10 \times B = 1{,}80{,}000 + 0.10B \]
  3. Step 3: Solve for \(B\)\[B - 0.10B = 1{,}80{,}000 \implies 0.90B = 1{,}80{,}000 \]\[B = \dfrac{1{,}80{,}000}{0.90} = 2{,}00{,}000 \text{ ₹} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: ₹2,00,000  |  Correct option: (A)

questions.question: In an Oedometer apparatus, a specimen of fully saturated clay has been consolidated under a vertical pressure of 50 kN/m² and is presently at equilibrium. The effective stress and pore water pressure immediately on increasing the vertical stress to 150 kN/m², respectively are
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Consolidation

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    • Fully saturated clay specimen
    • Initial vertical stress (at equilibrium): \(\sigma_0 = 50\text{ kN/m}^2\)
    • New total vertical stress: \(\sigma_1 = 150\text{ kN/m}^2\)
  • Aim: Find effective stress (\(\sigma'\)) and pore water pressure (\(u\)) immediately after increasing the vertical stress.

3. Core Concepts:

Effective Stress Principle (Terzaghi): \(\sigma = \sigma' + u\)

Undrained Loading: Immediately upon load application on a fully saturated clay, water cannot drain instantly. Since Skempton's pore pressure parameter \(B \approx 1\) for fully saturated clay, the entire increment in total stress is initially carried by pore water.\[\Delta u = B \cdot \Delta\sigma = 1 \times \Delta\sigma \]

Key Result: Effective stress does not change instantly under undrained loading.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Define initial equilibrium state.
  2. Calculate excess pore pressure generated by the load increment.
  3. Compute absolute conditions immediately post-loading.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Initial Equilibrium State
    • Total stress: \(\sigma_0 = 50\text{ kN/m}^2\)
    • Excess pore pressure: \(\Delta u_0 = 0\) (equilibrium)
    • Total pore pressure: \(u_0 = 0\text{ kN/m}^2\)
    • Effective stress: \(\sigma'_0 = 50 - 0 = 50\text{ kN/m}^2\)
  2. Step 2: Instantaneous Stress Changes\[\Delta\sigma = 150 - 50 = 100\text{ kN/m}^2 \]\[\Delta u = B \cdot \Delta\sigma = 1 \times 100 = 100\text{ kN/m}^2 \]
  3. Step 3: Immediate Post-Loading Values\[u = u_0 + \Delta u = 0 + 100 = 100\text{ kN/m}^2 \]\[\sigma'_1 = \sigma_1 - u = 150 - 100 = 50\text{ kN/m}^2 \](Effective stress remains unchanged immediately after undrained loading.)

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\sigma' = 50\text{ kN/m}^2\) and \(u = 100\text{ kN/m}^2\)  |  Correct option: (C)

questions.question: A partially-saturated soil sample has natural moisture content of 25% and bulk unit weight of 18.5 kN/m³. The specific gravity of soil solids is 2.65 and unit weight of water is 9.81 kN/m³. The unit weight of the soil sample on full saturation is
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Properties

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Natural moisture content, \(w = 25\% = 0.25\)
    • Bulk unit weight, \(\gamma_t = 18.5\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Specific gravity of solids, \(G_s = 2.65\)
    • Unit weight of water, \(\gamma_w = 9.81\text{ kN/m}^3\)
  • Aim: Determine the saturated unit weight (\(\gamma_{sat}\)) upon full saturation.

3. Core Concepts:

\[\gamma_d = \dfrac{\gamma_t}{1+w}, \qquad \gamma_d = \dfrac{G_s \gamma_w}{1+e}, \qquad \gamma_{sat} = \dfrac{(G_s + e)\gamma_w}{1+e} \]

questions.question: If water is flowing at the same depth in most hydraulically efficient triangular and rectangular channel sections then the ratio of hydraulic radius of triangular section to that of rectangular section is
questions.explanation:

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis / Recall
  • Given Data:
    • Most hydraulically efficient triangular channel section
    • Most hydraulically efficient rectangular channel section
    • Both flowing at the same depth (\(y\))
  • Aim: Ratio of hydraulic radius of the triangular section (\(R_{tri}\)) to that of the rectangular section (\(R_{rect}\)).

3. Core Concepts:

Hydraulic Radius: \(R = \dfrac{A}{P}\) where \(A\) is flow area and \(P\) is wetted perimeter.

Most Efficient Rectangular Section: Width \(B = 2y\)

Most Efficient Triangular Section: Vertex angle \(= 90^\circ\) (side slopes \(1\text{H}:1\text{V}\), i.e., \(m=1\))

4. Solution Method:

Calculate algebraic expressions for \(R\) for both efficient sections in terms of depth \(y\), then find the ratio.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: \(R_{rect}\) for Efficient Rectangular Channel
    • \(B = 2y\)
    • \(A_{rect} = 2y \times y = 2y^2\)
    • \(P_{rect} = 2y + 2y = 4y\)
    \[R_{rect} = \dfrac{2y^2}{4y} = \dfrac{y}{2} \]
  2. Step 2: \(R_{tri}\) for Efficient Triangular Channel
    • Side slope \(m = 1\), Top width \(T = 2y\)
    • \(A_{tri} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2y \times y = y^2\)
    • Slant side \(= \sqrt{y^2 + y^2} = \sqrt{2}\,y\)
    • \(P_{tri} = 2\sqrt{2}\,y\)
    \[R_{tri} = \dfrac{y^2}{2\sqrt{2}\,y} = \dfrac{y}{2\sqrt{2}} \]
  3. Step 3: Compute the Ratio\[\dfrac{R_{tri}}{R_{rect}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{y}{2\sqrt{2}}}{\dfrac{y}{2}} = \dfrac{y}{2\sqrt{2}} \times \dfrac{2}{y} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\)  |  Correct option: (A)

questions.question:
Consider the limit:
\[\lim_{x \to 1} \left( \dfrac{1}{\ln x} - \dfrac{1}{x - 1} \right) \]
The limit (correct up to one decimal place) is ___________
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Calculus

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: \(\displaystyle\lim_{x \to 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\ln x} - \dfrac{1}{x-1}\right)\)
  • Aim: Evaluate the limit correct to one decimal place.

3. Core Concepts:

Indeterminate Form: Substituting \(x = 1\) gives \(\dfrac{1}{0} - \dfrac{1}{0}\) → \(\infty - \infty\) form.

Resolution: Combine fractions and apply Taylor Series expansion around the limit point.

4. Solution Method:

Let \(x = 1 + h\). As \(x \to 1\), \(h \to 0\).\[L = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\dfrac{1}{\ln(1+h)} - \dfrac{1}{h}\right) = \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{h - \ln(1+h)}{h\ln(1+h)} \]

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Substitute Maclaurin series: \(\ln(1+h) = h - \dfrac{h^2}{2} + \dfrac{h^3}{3} - \cdots\)
  2. Numerator:\[h - \left(h - \dfrac{h^2}{2} + \dfrac{h^3}{3} - \cdots\right) = \dfrac{h^2}{2} - \dfrac{h^3}{3} + \cdots \]
  3. Denominator:\[h \times \left(h - \dfrac{h^2}{2} + \cdots\right) = h^2 - \dfrac{h^3}{2} + \cdots \]
  4. Divide numerator and denominator by \(h^2\):\[L = \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{h}{3} + \cdots}{1 - \dfrac{h}{2} + \cdots} = \dfrac{1/2}{1} = 0.5 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.5  |  Accepted key range: 0.5 to 0.5

  1. Integral over \(x\):\[ \int_{2}^{3} x\, dx = \left[\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right]_2^3 = \dfrac{9-4}{2} = \dfrac{5}{2} \]
  2. Integral over \(y\):\[ \int_{1}^{2} y\, dy = \left[\dfrac{y^2}{2}\right]_1^2 = \dfrac{4-1}{2} = \dfrac{3}{2} \]
  3. Integral over \(z\):\[ \int_{0}^{1} z\, dz = \left[\dfrac{z^2}{2}\right]_0^1 = \dfrac{1}{2} \]
  4. Final Result:\[I = 8 \times \dfrac{5}{2} \times \dfrac{3}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 8 \times \dfrac{15}{8} = 15 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 15  |  Accepted key range: 15 to 15

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q20
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: The absolute magnitude of the shear stress component \( \sigma_{xy} \) (in MPa, round off to one decimal place) in x-y coordinate system is ___________
questions.explanation:
Solid Mechanics | Principal Stresses & Strains

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Original x-y system: \(\sigma_{xx} = +40\text{ MPa}\) (tensile), \(\sigma_{yy} = +35.6\text{ MPa}\) (tensile), \(\tau_{xy}\) unknown
    • Transformed X-Y system: \(\sigma_{XX} = +120\text{ MPa}\) (tensile), \(\tau_{XY} = \pm50\text{ MPa}\)
    • Visual angle \(\theta \approx 30^\circ\) (graphical approximation only)
  • Aim: Find the absolute magnitude of shear stress \(|\tau_{xy}|\) in the original x-y system.

3. Core Concepts:

Stress Tensor Invariants: When a stress element is rotated, certain mathematical combinations of stress components remain constant.

First Invariant (\(I_1\)): Sum of normal stresses is constant.\[\sigma_{xx} + \sigma_{yy} = \sigma_{XX} + \sigma_{YY} \]

Second Invariant (\(I_2\)): Determinant of the stress tensor is constant.\[\sigma_{xx}\sigma_{yy} - \tau_{xy}^2 = \sigma_{XX}\sigma_{YY} - \tau_{XY}^2 \]

Key Insight: Using stress invariants entirely bypasses angle dependency and sign-convention errors (since shear stress is squared), neutralizing the ambiguity from the approximate visual angle. Applying rotation formulas directly with \(\theta = 30^\circ\) gives contradictory values.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Apply First Invariant to find \(\sigma_{YY}\)\[40 + 35.6 = 120 + \sigma_{YY} \implies \sigma_{YY} = 75.6 - 120 = -44.4\text{ MPa} \]
  2. Step 2: Apply Second Invariant\[(40)(35.6) - \tau_{xy}^2 = (120)(-44.4) - (50)^2 \]\[1424 - \tau_{xy}^2 = -5328 - 2500 = -7828 \]
  3. Step 3: Solve for \(|\tau_{xy}|\)\[\tau_{xy}^2 = 1424 + 7828 = 9252 \]\[|\tau_{xy}| = \sqrt{9252} \approx 96.2\text{ MPa} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 96.2 MPa  |  Accepted key range: 95 to 97

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q21
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
The equation of deformation is derived to be \( y = x^2 - xL \) for a beam shown in the figure.



The curvature of the beam at the mid-span (in units, in integer) will be ___________
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Deflection of Beams

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: Deflection curve equation: \(y = x^2 - xL\)
  • Aim: Find the curvature of the beam at mid-span (\(x = L/2\)).

3. Core Concepts:

Curvature (\(\kappa\)): For small lateral deflections in beam theory, curvature is approximated by the second derivative of the deflection equation.\[\kappa \approx \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} \]The exact formula is \(\kappa = \dfrac{y''}{[1+(y')^2]^{3/2}}\); since beam deflections are small, \((y')^2 \approx 0\), giving \(\kappa = y''\).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Differentiate \(y(x)\) once to find slope \(dy/dx\).
  2. Differentiate again to find curvature \(d^2y/dx^2\).
  3. Evaluate at \(x = L/2\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: First Derivative (Slope)\[y = x^2 - xL \implies \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x - L \]
  2. Step 2: Second Derivative (Curvature)\[\kappa = \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \dfrac{d}{dx}(2x - L) = 2 \]
  3. Step 3: Evaluate at Mid-span
    The second derivative is a constant — curvature is uniform throughout. At \(x = L/2\): \(\kappa = 2\).
    Verification using exact formula: slope at mid-span \(y' = 2(L/2) - L = 0\), so \(\kappa = 2/[1+0]^{3/2} = 2\). ✓

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 2  |  Accepted key range: 2 to 2

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q23
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: The cohesion (c), angle of internal friction (φ) and unit weight (γ) of a soil are 15 kPa, 20° and 17.5 kN/m³, respectively. The maximum depth of unsupported excavation in the soil (in m, round off to two decimal places) is ___________
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Earth Pressure & Retaining Walls

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Cohesion, \(c = 15\text{ kPa}\)
    • Angle of internal friction, \(\phi = 20^\circ\)
    • Unit weight of soil, \(\gamma = 17.5\text{ kN/m}^3\)
  • Aim: Find the maximum depth of unsupported excavation (\(H_c\)) in metres.

3. Core Concepts:

Active Earth Pressure (\(c\)-\(\phi\) soil, Rankine's):\[p_a = \gamma z K_a - 2c\sqrt{K_a} \]

Coefficient of Active Earth Pressure:\[K_a = \tan^2\left(45^\circ - \dfrac{\phi}{2}\right) \implies \sqrt{K_a} = \tan\left(45^\circ - \dfrac{\phi}{2}\right) \]

Critical Depth Formula: The maximum unsupported height equals twice the depth of the tension crack.\[H_c = \dfrac{4c}{\gamma\sqrt{K_a}} = \dfrac{4c}{\gamma}\tan\left(45^\circ + \dfrac{\phi}{2}\right) \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Compute \(\sqrt{K_a}\) using \(\phi = 20^\circ\).
  2. Substitute \(c\), \(\gamma\), and \(\sqrt{K_a}\) into the formula.
  3. Round to two decimal places.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Calculate \(\sqrt{K_a}\)\[\sqrt{K_a} = \tan\left(45^\circ - \dfrac{20^\circ}{2}\right) = \tan(35^\circ) \approx 0.7002 \]
  2. Step 2: Calculate \(H_c\)\[H_c = \dfrac{4 \times 15}{17.5 \times 0.7002} = \dfrac{60}{12.2535} = 4.8965\text{ m} \approx 4.90\text{ m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 4.90 m  |  Accepted key range: 4.80 to 5.00

questions.question:
Two reservoirs are connected through a homogeneous and isotropic aquifer having hydraulic conductivity (K) of 25 m/day and effective porosity (η) of 0.3 as shown in the figure (not to scale). Ground water is flowing in the aquifer at the steady state.



If water in Reservoir 1 is contaminated then the time (in days, round off to one decimal place) taken by the contaminated water to reach to Reservoir 2 will be ___________
questions.explanation:
Engineering Hydrology / Geotechnical Engineering | Groundwater Flow

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Hydraulic conductivity, \(K = 25\text{ m/day}\)
    • Effective porosity, \(\eta = 0.3\)
    • Head at Reservoir 1, \(h_1 = 30\text{ m}\)
    • Head at Reservoir 2, \(h_2 = 10\text{ m}\)
    • Horizontal distance between reservoirs \(= 2000\text{ m}\)
    • Aquifer dip angle \(= 10^\circ\)
  • Aim: Determine travel time for contaminated water from Reservoir 1 to Reservoir 2.

3. Core Concepts:

Darcy's Law: \(v = K \cdot i\) where \(i = \Delta h / L\)

Seepage Velocity: \(v_s = v / \eta\) (actual velocity through soil voids)

Travel Time: \(t = L / v_s = \eta L^2 / (K \Delta h)\)

Note on Setter's Intent: The true flow path length along the dipped aquifer is \(2000/\cos(10^\circ) = 2030.85\text{ m}\), giving \(t \approx 2475\text{ days}\). The official key expects 2400 days, indicating the setter used the horizontal projected distance \(L = 2000\text{ m}\) directly. We proceed accordingly.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Head Loss\[\Delta h = 30 - 10 = 20\text{ m} \]
  2. Step 2: Seepage Velocity\[i = \dfrac{20}{2000} = 0.01 \]\[v = 25 \times 0.01 = 0.25\text{ m/day} \]\[v_s = \dfrac{0.25}{0.3} = 0.8\overline{3}\text{ m/day} \]
  3. Step 3: Travel Time\[t = \dfrac{L}{v_s} = \dfrac{2000}{0.8333} = 2400\text{ days} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 2400 days  |  Accepted key range: 2400 to 2400

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q25
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question: A signalized intersection operates in two phases. The lost time is 3 seconds per phase. The maximum ratios of approach flow to saturation flow for the two phases are 0.37 and 0.40. The optimum cycle length using the Webster’s method (in seconds, round off to one decimal place) is ___________

Transportation Engineering | Traffic Signal Design

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Number of phases, \(n = 2\)
    • Lost time per phase, \(t_L = 3\text{ s}\)
    • Maximum flow ratio for phase 1, \(y_1 = 0.37\)
    • Maximum flow ratio for phase 2, \(y_2 = 0.40\)
  • Aim: Calculate the optimum cycle length (\(C_0\)) using Webster's formula.

3. Core Concepts:

Webster's Method: Minimizes total vehicular delay at a signalized intersection.

Total Lost Time: \(L = n \times t_L\)

Total Flow Ratio: \(Y = \sum y_i\)

Optimum Cycle Length:\[C_0 = \dfrac{1.5L + 5}{1 - Y} \]

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Total Lost Time\[L = 2 \times 3 = 6\text{ s} \]
  2. Step 2: Total Flow Ratio\[Y = 0.37 + 0.40 = 0.77 \]
  3. Step 3: Webster's Formula\[C_0 = \dfrac{1.5(6) + 5}{1 - 0.77} = \dfrac{9 + 5}{0.23} = \dfrac{14}{0.23} = 60.87\text{ s} \approx 60.9\text{ s} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 60.9 seconds  |  Accepted key range: 60.7 to 61.1

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q26
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: The solution of the second-order differential equation \( \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + 2\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = 0 \) with boundary conditions \( y(0) = 1 \) and \( y(1) = 3 \) is
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Differential Equations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Second-order linear differential equation: \(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + 2\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = 0\)
    • Boundary condition 1: \(y(0) = 1\)
    • Boundary condition 2: \(y(1) = 3\)
  • Aim: Find the particular solution \(y(x)\) that satisfies both the differential equation and the boundary conditions.

3. Core Concepts:

Linear Homogeneous ODEs: For an equation of the form \(ay'' + by' + cy = 0\), we substitute \(y = e^{mx}\) to obtain the characteristic (auxiliary) equation \(am^2 + bm + c = 0\).

Roots of Characteristic Equation: If roots \(m_1\) and \(m_2\) are real and equal (\(m_1 = m_2 = m\)), the general solution is:

\[y(x) = (C_1 + C_2 x)e^{mx} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Formulate the characteristic equation from the given differential equation.
  2. Find the roots of the characteristic equation.
  3. Write the general solution format based on the nature of the roots.
  4. Apply the first boundary condition \(y(0) = 1\) to find constant \(C_1\).
  5. Apply the second boundary condition \(y(1) = 3\) to find constant \(C_2\).
  6. Substitute \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) back into the general solution to obtain the final equation.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Write the auxiliary equation.\[m^2 + 2m + 1 = 0 \]
  2. Step 2: Solve for \(m\).\[(m + 1)^2 = 0 \implies m = -1 \text{ (Repeated roots)} \]
  3. Step 3: Form the general solution.\[y(x) = (C_1 + C_2 x)e^{-x} \]
  4. Step 4: Apply boundary condition \(y(0) = 1\).\[y(0) = (C_1 + C_2(0))e^{0} \]\[1 = C_1 \cdot 1 \implies C_1 = 1 \]So, the equation updates to: \(y(x) = (1 + C_2 x)e^{-x}\)
  5. Step 5: Apply boundary condition \(y(1) = 3\).\[y(1) = (1 + C_2(1))e^{-1} \]\[3 = \dfrac{1 + C_2}{e} \]\[3e = 1 + C_2 \implies C_2 = 3e - 1 \]
  6. Step 6: Substitute constants into the general solution.\[y(x) = (1 + (3e - 1)x)e^{-x} \]Expanding this yields:\[y(x) = e^{-x} + (3e - 1)xe^{-x} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(e^{-x} + (3e - 1)xe^{-x}\)  |  Correct option: (A)

questions.question: The value of \( \displaystyle \int_0^1 e^x dx \) using the trapezoidal rule with four equal subintervals is
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Numerical Methods

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Integral to evaluate: \(\displaystyle\int_0^1 e^x\, dx\)
    • Method: Trapezoidal Rule
    • Number of equal subintervals (\(n\)): \(4\)
  • Aim: Calculate the numerical value of the integral using the specified numerical method.

3. Core Concepts:

Step Size (\(h\)): Calculated as \(h = \dfrac{b - a}{n}\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are the lower and upper limits.

Trapezoidal Rule Formula:

\[ I = \dfrac{h}{2} \left[y_0 + y_n + 2(y_1 + y_2 + \dots + y_{n-1}) \right] \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate the step size \(h\).
  2. Determine the discrete \(x\) values (nodes) from \(a\) to \(b\).
  3. Compute the corresponding \(y\) values (\(y = e^x\)) for each node.
  4. Apply the Trapezoidal rule formula taking care not to prematurely round intermediate values to ensure precision.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Calculate step size.\[h = \dfrac{1 - 0}{4} = 0.25 \]
  2. Steps 2 & 3: Generate nodes and evaluate \(y = e^x\).
    \(x_i\)\(y_i = e^{x_i}\)
    \(x_0 = 0.00\)\(y_0 = 1.0000\)
    \(x_1 = 0.25\)\(y_1 \approx 1.2840\)
    \(x_2 = 0.50\)\(y_2 \approx 1.6487\)
    \(x_3 = 0.75\)\(y_3 \approx 2.1170\)
    \(x_4 = 1.00\)\(y_4 \approx 2.7183\)
  3. Step 4: Apply the Trapezoidal rule.\[ I = \dfrac{0.25}{2} \left[y_0 + y_4 + 2(y_1 + y_2 + y_3) \right] \]\[ I = 0.125 \left[1.0000 + 2.7183 + 2(1.2840 + 1.6487 + 2.1170) \right] \]\[ I = 0.125 \left[3.7183 + 2(5.0497) \right] \]\[ I = 0.125 \left[3.7183 + 10.0994 \right] \]\[I = 0.125 \times 13.8177 \]\[I \approx 1.7272 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(1.727\)  |  Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q28
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: A 50 mL sample of industrial wastewater is taken into a silica crucible. The empty weight of the crucible is 54.352 g. The crucible with the sample is dried in a hot air oven at 104 °C till a constant weight of 55.129 g. Thereafter, the crucible with the dried sample is fired at 600 °C for 1 h in a muffle furnace, and the weight of the crucible along with residue is determined as 54.783 g. The concentration of total volatile solids is ___________.
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Wastewater Quality

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Sample volume (\(V\)) = \(50 \text{ mL}\) = \(0.050 \text{ L}\)
    • Weight of empty crucible (\(W_{\text{empty}}\)) = \(54.352 \text{ g}\)
    • Weight of crucible + sample dried at 104°C (\(W_{104}\)) = \(55.129 \text{ g}\)
    • Weight of crucible + residue fired at 600°C (\(W_{600}\)) = \(54.783 \text{ g}\)
  • Aim: Determine the concentration of Total Volatile Solids (TVS) in \(\text{mg/L}\).

3. Core Concepts:

Total Solids (TS): The residue left after drying a sample at 104°C. It includes both volatile (organic) and fixed (inorganic) solids.

Total Fixed Solids (TFS): The residue remaining after igniting the dried sample at 600°C in a muffle furnace.

Total Volatile Solids (TVS): The portion of Total Solids that volatilizes (burns off) at 600°C.\[W_{\text{TVS}} = W_{104} - W_{600} \]

Concentration: Mass of target constituent divided by the initial volume of the sample.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate the mass of Total Volatile Solids in grams by subtracting the fired weight from the dried weight.
  2. Convert the mass from grams (g) to milligrams (mg).
  3. Convert the sample volume from milliliters (mL) to Liters (L).
  4. Divide the mass in mg by the volume in L to get the concentration in mg/L.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Calculate the mass of Volatile Solids.\[W_{\text{TVS}} = W_{104} - W_{600} = 55.129 \text{ g} - 54.783 \text{ g} = 0.346 \text{ g} \]
  2. Step 2: Convert mass to mg.\[\text{Mass} = 0.346 \text{ g} \times 1000 \text{ mg/g} = 346 \text{ mg} \]
  3. Step 3: Convert volume to L.\[V = 50 \text{ mL} = 50 \times 10^{-3} \text{ L} = 0.050 \text{ L} \]
  4. Step 4: Calculate Concentration.\[\text{Concentration of TVS} = \dfrac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Volume}} = \dfrac{346 \text{ mg}}{0.050 \text{ L}} = 6920 \text{ mg/L} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(6920 \text{ mg/L}\)  |  Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q29
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
A wedge M and a block N are subjected to forces P and Q as shown in the figure. If force P is sufficiently large, then the block N can be raised. The weights of the wedge and the block are negligible compared to the forces P and Q. The coefficient of friction (μ) along the inclined surface between the wedge and the block is 0.2. All other surfaces are frictionless. The wedge angle is 30°.



The limiting force P, in terms of Q, required for impending motion of block N to just move it in the upward direction is given as \( P = \alpha Q \). The value of the coefficient ‘α’ (round off to one decimal place) is
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mechanics | Statics & Friction

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Wedge angle (\(\theta\)) = \(30^\circ\)
    • Coefficient of friction on inclined surface (\(\mu\)) = \(0.2\)
    • All other surfaces (1 and 3) are frictionless.
    • Force \(P\) is applied horizontally to Wedge M.
    • Force \(Q\) is applied vertically to Block N.
    • Weights of wedge and block are negligible.
  • Aim: Find the coefficient \(\alpha\) in the relation \(P = \alpha Q\) for the impending upward motion of block N.

3. Core Concepts:

Impending Motion & Friction Direction: When block N is about to move up, it slides up the inclined surface relative to wedge M (because wedge M is moving left, pushing N upwards). Therefore, friction on Block N acts down the incline.

Action-Reaction Pairs: The normal force and friction force exerted by Wedge M on Block N are equal and opposite to those exerted by Block N on Wedge M.

Static Equilibrium: \(\sum F_x = 0\) and \(\sum F_y = 0\) for free-body diagrams of both components.

Wedge Friction Equation: For a horizontal force driving a wedge to lift a vertical load against a vertical wall, the relation maps directly to \(P = Q\tan(\theta + \phi)\), where \(\phi\) is the angle of friction (\(\tan\phi = \mu\)).

4. Solution Method:

  1. FBD of Block N: Resolve forces vertically to express the normal force (\(N_2\)) between the block and wedge in terms of the load \(Q\).
  2. FBD of Wedge M: Resolve forces horizontally to express the driving force \(P\) in terms of the normal force \(N_2\) and friction.
  3. Combine the two equations to eliminate \(N_2\) and find the ratio \(P/Q\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Analyze forces on Block N (Vertical Equilibrium)
    • Upward force: Vertical component of normal force \(N_2\cos 30^\circ\)
    • Downward forces: Load \(Q\) and vertical component of friction \(f_2 = \mu N_2 \sin 30^\circ\)
    \[\sum F_y = 0 \implies N_2 \cos 30^\circ - \mu N_2 \sin 30^\circ - Q = 0 \]\[N_2 (\cos 30^\circ - 0.2\sin 30^\circ) = Q \]\[N_2 = \dfrac{Q}{\cos 30^\circ - 0.2\sin 30^\circ} \]
  2. Step 2: Analyze forces on Wedge M (Horizontal Equilibrium)
    • Leftward force: Driving force \(P\)
    • Rightward forces: Horizontal component of normal reaction \(N_2\sin 30^\circ\) and horizontal component of friction \(\mu N_2 \cos 30^\circ\) (friction on the wedge acts up the incline)
    \[\sum F_x = 0 \implies P = N_2 \sin 30^\circ + \mu N_2 \cos 30^\circ \]\[P = N_2 (\sin 30^\circ + 0.2\cos 30^\circ) \]
  3. Step 3: Substitute \(N_2\) and solve for \(P/Q\)\[P = Q \left( \dfrac{\sin 30^\circ + 0.2\cos 30^\circ}{\cos 30^\circ - 0.2\sin 30^\circ} \right) \]Dividing numerator and denominator by \(\cos 30^\circ\):\[P = Q \left( \dfrac{\tan 30^\circ + 0.2}{1 - 0.2\tan 30^\circ} \right) \](Note: This is strictly mathematically equivalent to \(P = Q\tan(30^\circ + \phi)\))

    Substituting values (\(\tan 30^\circ = 0.57735\)):\[P = Q \left( \dfrac{0.57735 + 0.2}{1 - 0.2 \times 0.57735} \right) = Q \left( \dfrac{0.77735}{1 - 0.11547} \right) = Q \left( \dfrac{0.77735}{0.88453} \right) \approx 0.8788\, Q \]
  4. Step 4: Rounding
    The coefficient \(\alpha\) is requested rounded to one decimal place.\[\alpha = 0.9 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\alpha = 0.9\)  |  Correct option: (D)

  • Given Data:

    • Total number of historical bids = \(6 + 12 + 3 + 6 + 3 = 30\)
    • Contractor X's mark-up for the next project = \(8\%\) of cost.
  • Aim: Calculate the probability of Contractor X winning the bid against Contractor Y.

3. Core Concepts:

Winning Criterion: In a standard competitive bidding process, the contractor with the lowest bid wins. Thus, Contractor X wins if \(\text{Bid}_X < \text{Bid}_Y\).

Bid Formulation: \(\text{Bid} = \text{Cost} + \text{Markup}\)

questions.question: A fluid flowing steadily in a circular pipe of radius R has a velocity that is everywhere parallel to the axis (centerline) of the pipe. questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Flow Through Pipes

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Derivation
  • Given Data:
    • Velocity profile for steady flow in a circular pipe: \(V_r = U\left(1 - \dfrac{r^2}{R^2}\right)\)
    • \(R\) = radius of the pipe
    • \(U\) = maximum velocity (at center \(r = 0\))
  • Aim: Determine the average velocity of the fluid in terms of \(U\).

3. Core Concepts:

Average Velocity (\(V_{avg}\)): Defined as total discharge (\(Q\)) divided by the total cross-sectional area (\(A\)).\[V_{avg} = \dfrac{Q}{A} \]

Discharge (\(Q\)) Integration: Discharge is the integral of velocity over the cross-sectional area. For an axisymmetric circular pipe, a differential ring element has area \(dA = 2\pi r\, dr\).\[Q = \int_{0}^{R} V_r\, dA = \int_{0}^{R} V_r\,(2\pi r\, dr) \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Setup the integral for discharge \(Q\) using the given velocity profile \(V_r\).
  2. Integrate with respect to \(r\) from \(0\) to \(R\).
  3. Divide the computed discharge \(Q\) by the pipe's cross-sectional area \(A = \pi R^2\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Formulate the integral for total discharge \(Q\).\[Q = \int_{0}^{R} U\left(1 - \dfrac{r^2}{R^2}\right) 2\pi r\, dr \]
  2. Step 2: Expand the integrand.\[Q = 2\pi U \int_{0}^{R} \left(r - \dfrac{r^3}{R^2}\right) dr \]
  3. Step 3: Perform the definite integration.\[ Q = 2\pi U \left[\dfrac{r^2}{2} - \dfrac{r^4}{4R^2} \right]_{0}^{R} \]Substituting the upper limit \(R\) and lower limit \(0\):\[Q = 2\pi U \left( \dfrac{R^2}{2} - \dfrac{R^4}{4R^2} \right) = 2\pi U \left( \dfrac{R^2}{2} - \dfrac{R^2}{4} \right) = 2\pi U \left( \dfrac{R^2}{4} \right) = \dfrac{\pi R^2 U}{2} \]
  4. Step 4: Calculate average velocity.\[A = \pi R^2 \]\[V_{avg} = \dfrac{Q}{A} = \dfrac{\dfrac{\pi R^2 U}{2}}{\pi R^2} = \dfrac{U}{2} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\dfrac{U}{2}\)  |  Correct option: (A)

    • pH governs their proportion.

3. Core Concepts:

Acid-Base Equilibrium: Ammonia in water undergoes the following reversible dissociation reaction:\[NH_4^+ \rightleftharpoons NH_3 + H^+ \]

Dissociation Constant (\(K_a\)): The equilibrium is described by \(K_a = \dfrac{[NH_3][H^+]}{[NH_4^+]}\). For the ammonium ion at standard temperature (\(25^\circ\text{C}\)), \(pK_a \approx 9.25\).

Henderson-Hasselbalch Equation:\[ pH = pK_a + \log_{10}\left(\dfrac{[NH_3]}{[NH_4^+]}\right) \]

  • If \(pH = pK_a = 9.25\), then \(\log\left(\dfrac{[NH_3]}{[NH_4^+]}\right) = 0 \implies [NH_3] = [NH_4^+]\).
  • If \(pH < 9.25\): excess \(H^+\) shifts equilibrium left, favoring \(NH_4^+\).
  • If \(pH > 9.25\): basic environment shifts equilibrium right, favoring \(NH_3\).

4. Solution Method:

Evaluate each statement against the equilibrium rules and identify the correct one.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  • Option (A): "At pH above 9.25, only \(NH_4^+\) will be present." → Incorrect. \(NH_3\) predominates above \(pK_a\). Also, "only" is chemically inaccurate as equilibrium maintains trace amounts of both.
  • Option (B): "At pH below 9.25, \(NH_3\) will be predominant." → Incorrect. Below 9.25, \(NH_4^+\) predominates.
  • Option (C): "At pH 7.0, \(NH_4^+\) and \(NH_3\) will be found in equal measures." → Incorrect. Equal measures occur exactly at \(pH = pK_a \approx 9.25\).
  • Option (D): "At pH 7.0, \(NH_4^+\) will be predominant." → Correct. Since \(7.0 \ll 9.25\):\[ \dfrac{[NH_3]}{[NH_4^+]} = 10^{(7.0 - 9.25)} \approx 0.0056 \]Thus, \(NH_4^+\) heavily dominates (\(>99\%\)).

6. Final Answer:

Correct option: (D)

questions.question: On a road, the speed – density relationship of a traffic stream is given by \( u = 70 - 0.7k \) (where speed, u, is in km/h and density, k, is in veh/km). At the capacity condition, the average time headway will be
questions.explanation:
Transportation Engineering | Traffic Engineering

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Speed-density relationship: \(u = 70 - 0.7k\)
    • \(u\) = speed in \(\text{km/h}\)
    • \(k\) = density in \(\text{veh/km}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the average time headway (in seconds) at the capacity condition.

3. Core Concepts:

Greenshields Macroscopic Model: The linear speed-density relationship follows the form \(u = u_f - \left(\dfrac{u_f}{k_j}\right)k\), where \(u_f\) is free-flow speed and \(k_j\) is jam density.

Traffic Flow Equation: Flow (\(q\)) is the product of speed and density.\[q = u \times k \]

Capacity (\(q_{max}\)): Maximum traffic flow occurs when \(\dfrac{dq}{dk} = 0\). For a linear Greenshields model, capacity occurs at \(u_c = \dfrac{u_f}{2}\) and \(k_c = \dfrac{k_j}{2}\).

Time Headway (\(h_t\)): The average time interval between successive vehicles; it is the reciprocal of the traffic flow.\[h_t = \dfrac{1}{q} \]If \(q\) is in \(\text{veh/hr}\), then \(h_t\) in seconds is \(h_t = \dfrac{3600}{q}\).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Formulate the equation for traffic flow \(q\) in terms of density \(k\).
  2. Maximize \(q\) by differentiating with respect to \(k\) and setting it to zero to find the capacity (\(q_{max}\)).
  3. Calculate the time headway at capacity using \(h_t = \dfrac{3600}{q_{max}}\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Establish flow equation.\[q = u \cdot k = (70 - 0.7k)k = 70k - 0.7k^2 \]
  2. Step 2: Maximize flow to find capacity.\[\dfrac{dq}{dk} = 70 - 1.4k = 0 \]\[1.4k = 70 \implies k_c = \dfrac{70}{1.4} = 50\text{ veh/km} \]
  3. Step 3: Calculate capacity (\(q_{max}\)).\[q_{max} = 70(50) - 0.7(50)^2 = 3500 - 0.7(2500) = 3500 - 1750 = 1750\text{ veh/hr} \]Alternative check: \(u_c = 70 - 0.7(50) = 35\text{ km/h}\), so \(q_{max} = u_c \times k_c = 35 \times 50 = 1750\text{ veh/hr}\).
  4. Step 4: Calculate average time headway (\(h_t\)).\[h_t = \dfrac{3600\text{ s/hr}}{q_{max}\text{ veh/hr}} = \dfrac{3600}{1750} \approx 2.057\text{ s} \]
  5. Step 5: Match with options. The closest value is \(2.1\text{ s}\).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(2.1\text{ s}\)  |  Correct option: (D)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Load \(F = 10\sqrt{3}\text{ kN}\) at node T
    • Cross-sectional area \(A = 10^4\text{ mm}^2 = 0.01\text{ m}^2\)
    • Moment of Inertia \(I = 8.33 \times 10^6\text{ mm}^4\) (Distractor — joints in a truss are pinned; flexural rigidity is irrelevant for primary axial stresses)
    • Length \(L = 2\text{ m}\) for all members
    • Member Q-R has area = \(2A\)
  • Aim: Determine the compressive stress (in \(\text{kN/m}^2\)) in member Q-R.

3. Core Concepts:

Truss Geometry: Since all members have length \(L = 2\text{ m}\), the truss is composed of three identical equilateral triangles (\(\Delta PQT,\, \Delta QRT,\, \Delta SRT\)) with internal angles \(= 60^\circ\) and height \(h = L\sin(60^\circ) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}L\).

Method of Sections: A technique to find internal axial forces by cutting the truss into two free bodies and applying equilibrium conditions (\(\sum F = 0,\; \sum M = 0\)).

Axial Stress: \(\sigma = \dfrac{\text{Internal Force}}{\text{Cross-sectional Area}}\). Note that Q-R has area \(2A\), not \(A\).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine the support reaction at P using global symmetry.
  2. Pass a vertical imaginary section cutting members QR, QT, and PT.
  3. Consider the left free body and apply moment equilibrium about node T to isolate the force in QR (\(F_{QR}\)).
  4. Calculate the stress using the correct area for member QR (\(2A\)).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Geometric Properties and Reactions
    Height: \(h = 2\sin(60^\circ) = \sqrt{3}\text{ m}\)
    By geometric and loading symmetry:\[R_P = R_S = \dfrac{F}{2} = \dfrac{10\sqrt{3}}{2} = 5\sqrt{3}\text{ kN (upwards)} \]
  2. Step 2: Method of Sections
    Cut vertically through QR, QT, and PT. Consider the left part of the truss (nodes P and Q).
    Taking moments about node T (eliminates \(F_{QT}\) and \(F_{PT}\) since their lines of action pass through T):\[\sum M_T = 0 \implies -(R_P \times L_{PT}) - (F_{QR} \times h) = 0 \]\[-(5\sqrt{3} \times 2) - (F_{QR} \times \sqrt{3}) = 0 \]\[-10\sqrt{3} = F_{QR} \times \sqrt{3} \implies F_{QR} = -10\text{ kN} \]The negative sign confirms member Q-R is in compression with a force of \(10\text{ kN}\).

    • Beam type: Cantilever, Span \(L = 1.5\text{ m}\) (fixed end on the left)
    • Cross-section: \(b = 200\text{ mm}\), \(d = 300\text{ mm}\)
    • Tendon location: \(d_c = 50\text{ mm}\) from the top fiber
    • Prestressing force \((P_0)\) = \(50\text{ kN}\)
    • External load \((P)\) = \(5\text{ kN}\) concentrated at the free end
    • Point Q: Located at the top fiber of the fixed support (maximum moment location)
  • Aim: Find the resultant longitudinal stress at point Q in MPa.

3. Core Concepts:

Sign Convention: Compression is Positive (+), Tension is Negative (−). (Standard IS 1343 convention for prestressed concrete).

Cross-sectional Properties: Area \(A = b \times d\)    Section Modulus \(Z = \dfrac{bd^2}{6}\)

Stress due to Prestress (\(P_0\)):

  • Axial compression \(= +\dfrac{P_0}{A}\)
  • The tendon is above the neutral axis (eccentricity \(e\)), creating an internal moment \(M_p = P_0 \times e\) that bends the beam upwards, putting top fibers in additional compression.

Stress due to External Load (\(P\)):

  • Downward point load on a cantilever creates a hogging moment at the support (\(M_e = P \times L\)).
  • Hogging moment puts the top fibers in tension.

Superposition Principle: \(\sigma_{\text{Resultant}} = \sigma_{\text{Axial}} + \sigma_{\text{Bending (Prestress)}} + \sigma_{\text{Bending (External)}}\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate cross-sectional properties (\(A, Z\)).
  2. Determine eccentricity (\(e\)) of the tendon from the Neutral Axis.
  3. Calculate stresses at the top fiber at the fixed support due to prestress.
  4. Calculate stresses at the same point due to the external load.
  5. Sum the stresses to find the resultant. (Self-weight neglected as concrete density is not provided.)

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Section Properties\[A = 200 \times 300 = 60{,}000\text{ mm}^2 \]\[Z_{top} = \dfrac{200 \times 300^2}{6} = 3{,}000{,}000\text{ mm}^3 = 3 \times 10^6\text{ mm}^3 \]Distance of Neutral Axis from top \(= \dfrac{d}{2} = 150\text{ mm}\)
    Eccentricity \(e = 150 - 50 = 100\text{ mm}\) (above NA)
  2. Step 2: Stresses due to Prestressing at Top Fiber (Point Q)
    Direct stress:\[+\dfrac{P_0}{A} = +\dfrac{50 \times 10^3}{60{,}000} = +0.833\text{ MPa} \]Prestress moment: \(M_p = P_0 \times e = 50 \times 10^3 \times 100 = 5 \times 10^6\text{ N·mm}\)
    Bending stress due to \(M_p\):\[+\dfrac{M_p}{Z} = +\dfrac{5 \times 10^6}{3 \times 10^6} = +1.667\text{ MPa} \]Total prestress stress at Q \(= 0.833 + 1.667 = +2.500\text{ MPa}\) (Compression)
  3. Step 3: Stresses due to External Load at Top Fiber (Point Q)
    Bending moment at fixed end: \(M_e = P \times L = 5 \times 1.5 = 7.5\text{ kN·m} = 7.5 \times 10^6\text{ N·mm}\)
    Bending stress due to \(M_e\):\[-\dfrac{M_e}{Z} = -\dfrac{7.5 \times 10^6}{3 \times 10^6} = -2.500\text{ MPa (Tension)} \]
  4. Step 4: Resultant Stress\[\sigma_{\text{Resultant}} = (+2.500) + (-2.500) = 0\text{ MPa} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0 MPa  |  Accepted key range: 0 to 0

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q40
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Steel Tension, Compression Members & Plastic Analysis
questions.question:
A column is subjected to a total load (P) of 60 kN supported through a bracket connection, as shown in the figure (not to scale).



The resultant force in bolt R (in kN, round off to one decimal place) is ___________
questions.explanation:
Design of Steel Structures | Eccentric Bolted Connections

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Total applied load, \(P = 60\text{ kN}\)
    • Arrangement: 2 columns of 3 bolts each. Total bolts, \(n = 6\)
    • Pitch, \(p = 30\text{ mm}\) (vertical distance between bolts)
    • Gauge, \(g = 40 + 40 = 80\text{ mm}\) (horizontal distance between bolt columns)
  • Aim: Find the resultant force in bolt R (middle bolt in the right column) in kN.
  • Sanity Check & Correction Note: Visual Ambiguity: The left witness line for the \(100\text{ mm}\) dimension appears to align with the right column of bolts. If taken literally, the eccentricity from the CG would be \(140\text{ mm}\), leading to an answer outside the official key. Matching the official range (27.0–29.0 kN) requires \(100\text{ mm}\) to be the eccentricity \(e\) measured directly from the Center of Gravity (CG) of the bolt group. We proceed with \(e = 100\text{ mm}\) from the CG.

3. Core Concepts:

According to the Elastic Method for in-plane eccentric connections (IS 800:2007):

  • Direct Shear Force (\(F_D\)): Primary load shared equally among all bolts.\[F_D = \dfrac{P}{n} \]
  • Torsional Shear Force (\(F_T\)): Moment \(M = P \times e\) causes a rotational force on each bolt proportional to its radial distance \(r\) from the CG.\[F_T = \dfrac{M \times r}{\sum r^2} \]
  • Resultant Force (\(F_R\)): Vector addition of \(F_D\) and \(F_T\).

4. Solution Method & Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Calculate \(\sum r^2\)
    The CG of the 6-bolt group is exactly midway between the two columns and the middle row.
    • 4 Corner bolts: \(x = \pm 40\text{ mm}\), \(y = \pm 30\text{ mm}\)\[r_{\text{corner}}^2 = 40^2 + 30^2 = 1600 + 900 = 2500\text{ mm}^2 \]
    • 2 Middle bolts (including Bolt R): \(x = \pm 40\text{ mm}\), \(y = 0\)\[r_{\text{mid}}^2 = 40^2 + 0^2 = 1600\text{ mm}^2 \]
    \[\sum r^2 = 4(2500) + 2(1600) = 10000 + 3200 = 13200\text{ mm}^2 \]
  2. Step 2: Calculate Direct Shear (\(F_D\))\[F_D = \dfrac{60\text{ kN}}{6} = 10\text{ kN} \]Direction: Downward (parallel to \(P\)).
  3. Step 3: Calculate Torsional Shear on Bolt R (\(F_T\))
    Bolt R is at the middle-right position with radial distance \(r = 40\text{ mm}\).
    Moment: \(M = P \times e = 60\text{ kN} \times 100\text{ mm} = 6000\text{ kN·mm}\)\[F_T = \dfrac{6000 \times 40}{13200} = \dfrac{240000}{13200} = 18.18\text{ kN} \]Direction: A downward load \(P\) on the right side causes a clockwise moment. For bolt R on the positive x-axis, clockwise rotation induces a strictly downward tangential force.
  4. Step 4: Calculate Resultant Force (\(F_R\))
    Since both \(F_D\) and \(F_T\) act vertically downward on Bolt R:\[F_R = F_D + F_T = 10 + 18.18 = 28.18\text{ kN} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 28.2 kN  |  Accepted key range: 27.0 to 29.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q41
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
Employ stiffness matrix approach for the simply supported beam as shown in the figure to calculate unknown displacements/rotations. Take length, \( L = 8 \) m; modulus of elasticity, \( E = 3 \times 10^4 \) N/mm²; moment of inertia, \( I = 225 \times 10^6 \) mm⁴.



The mid-span deflection of the beam (in mm, round off to integer) under \( P = 100 \) kN in downward direction will be ___________
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Matrix Method of Analysis

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Total length \(L = 8\text{ m}\) (two segments of \(l = 4\text{ m}\))
    • \(E = 3 \times 10^4\text{ N/mm}^2\)
    • \(I = 225 \times 10^6\text{ mm}^4\)
    • Segment AB: Rigidity \(= 2EI\); Segment BC: Rigidity \(= EI\)
    • Mid-span Load \(P = 100\text{ kN}\) (downward at node B)
  • Aim: Compute the mid-span deflection at node B using the stiffness matrix approach.

3. Core Concepts:

Treating B as a free node with two degrees of freedom (DOFs):

  • \(U_1\): Vertical downward deflection at B
  • \(U_2\): Clockwise rotation at B

Nodes A and C are pinned. For a member pinned at the far end, condensed stiffness coefficients simplify the matrix.

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Formulate the Global Stiffness Matrix \([K]\) at Node B
    For a member of length \(l\), pinned at the far end and continuous at B, applying unit displacements:

    Member AB (\(l = 4\text{ m}\), Rigidity \(= 2EI\)):
    • Apply \(U_1 = 1\): Force \(= \dfrac{3(2EI)}{l^3}\), Moment \(= -\dfrac{3(2EI)}{l^2}\)
    • Apply \(U_2 = 1\): Force \(= -\dfrac{3(2EI)}{l^2}\), Moment \(= \dfrac{3(2EI)}{l}\)
    Member BC (\(l = 4\text{ m}\), Rigidity \(= EI\)):
    • Apply \(U_1 = 1\): Force \(= \dfrac{3EI}{l^3}\), Moment \(= +\dfrac{3EI}{l^2}\)
    • Apply \(U_2 = 1\): Force \(= +\dfrac{3EI}{l^2}\), Moment \(= \dfrac{3EI}{l}\)
    Superimposing contributions \(K = K^{AB} + K^{BC}\):\[K_{11} = \dfrac{6EI}{l^3} + \dfrac{3EI}{l^3} = \dfrac{9EI}{l^3} \]\[K_{12} = K_{21} = -\dfrac{6EI}{l^2} + \dfrac{3EI}{l^2} = -\dfrac{3EI}{l^2} \]\[K_{22} = \dfrac{6EI}{l} + \dfrac{3EI}{l} = \dfrac{9EI}{l} \]
  2. Step 2: Solve the System \([K]\{U\} = \{F\}\)
    Load vector at B: \(\{F\} = \begin{bmatrix} P \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}\)\[ \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{9EI}{l^3} & -\dfrac{3EI}{l^2} \\[8pt] -\dfrac{3EI}{l^2} & \dfrac{9EI}{l} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} U_1 \\ U_2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} P \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} \]From the second row:\[-\dfrac{3EI}{l^2}U_1 + \dfrac{9EI}{l}U_2 = 0 \implies U_2 = \dfrac{1}{3l}U_1 \]Substituting into the first row:\[\dfrac{9EI}{l^3}U_1 - \dfrac{3EI}{l^2}\left(\dfrac{1}{3l}U_1\right) = P \implies \left(\dfrac{9EI}{l^3} - \dfrac{EI}{l^3}\right)U_1 = P \implies \dfrac{8EI}{l^3}U_1 = P \]\[U_1 = \dfrac{Pl^3}{8EI} \]
  3. Step 3: Insert Values and Calculate
    Converting to consistent units (N, mm):
    • \(P = 100\text{ kN} = 100{,}000\text{ N}\)
    • \(l = 4\text{ m} = 4000\text{ mm}\)
    • \(EI = 3 \times 10^4 \times 225 \times 10^6 = 6.75 \times 10^{12}\text{ N·mm}^2\)
    \[U_1 = \dfrac{100{,}000 \times (4000)^3}{8 \times 6.75 \times 10^{12}} = \dfrac{10^5 \times 64 \times 10^9}{54 \times 10^{12}} = \dfrac{6.4 \times 10^{15}}{5.4 \times 10^{13}} = \dfrac{6400}{54} \approx 118.5\text{ mm} \]Rounding to the nearest integer: \(U_1 = 119\text{ mm}\).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 119 mm  |  Accepted key range: 100 to 130

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q42

questions.question:
A square plate O-P-Q-R of a linear elastic material with sides 1.0 m is loaded in a state of plane stress. Under a given stress condition, the plate deforms to a new configuration O-P'-Q'-R' as shown in the figure (not to scale). Under the given deformation, the edges of the plate remain straight.



The horizontal displacement of the point (0.5 m, 0.5 m) in the plate O-P-Q-R (in mm, round off to one decimal place) is ___________
questions.explanation:
Solid Mechanics | Plane Stress & Deformation Geometry

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Synthesis
  • Given Data:
    • Linear elastic material square plate, side \(= 1.0\text{ m} = 1000\text{ mm}\)
    • Original coordinates: \(O(0,0)\), \(P(1000, 0)\), \(Q(1000, 1000)\), \(R(0, 1000)\)
    • Edges of the plate remain straight after deformation.
    • Extracted displacements from figure:
      • At \(O\): \(u_O = 0\text{ mm}\) (origin fixed)
      • At \(P\): \(u_P = +20\text{ mm}\) (horizontal shift)
      • At \(Q\): \(u_Q = -10\text{ mm}\) (\(Q'\) moved leftward relative to original vertical edge)
      • At \(R\): \(u_R = 0\text{ mm}\) (\(R'\) remains aligned with y-axis)
  • Aim: Find the horizontal displacement \(u(x,y)\) at the center point \((500, 500)\) in mm.

3. Core Concepts:

Because the plate edges remain straight during deformation, the horizontal displacement field \(u(x, y)\) can be modeled exactly using a Bilinear Shape Function:

\[u(x, y) = a_0 + a_1 x + a_2 y + a_3 xy \]

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Set up Boundary Condition Equations
    1. At \(O(0,0)\), \(u = 0\): \(\implies a_0 = 0\)
    2. At \(P(1000, 0)\), \(u = 20\text{ mm}\):\[a_1(1000) = 20 \implies a_1 = 0.02 \]
    3. At \(R(0, 1000)\), \(u = 0\text{ mm}\):\[a_2(1000) = 0 \implies a_2 = 0 \]
    4. At \(Q(1000, 1000)\), \(u = -10\text{ mm}\):\[a_1(1000) + a_2(1000) + a_3(1000 \times 1000) = -10 \]\[0.02(1000) + 0 + a_3(10^6) = -10 \implies 20 + 10^6 a_3 = -10 \implies a_3 = -3 \times 10^{-5} \]
  2. Step 2: Calculate Displacement at Point (500, 500)\[u(500, 500) = 0.02(500) + 0(500) + (-3 \times 10^{-5})(500 \times 500) \]\[u(500, 500) = 10 - (3 \times 10^{-5} \times 250{,}000) = 10 - 7.5 = 2.5\text{ mm} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 2.5 mm  |  Accepted key range: 2.4 to 2.6
