questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q44
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
The soil profile at a construction site is shown in the figure (not to scale). Ground water table (GWT) is at 5 m below the ground level at present. An old well data shows that the ground water table was as low as 10 m below the ground level in the past. Take unit weight of water, \( \gamma_w = 9.81 \) kN/m³.



The overconsolidation ratio (OCR) (round off to two decimal places) at the mid-point of the clay layer is ___________
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Consolidation (Overconsolidation Ratio)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Current Ground Water Table (GWT) depth = \(5\text{ m}\)
    • Past maximum GWT depth = \(10\text{ m}\)
    • \(\gamma_w = 9.81\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Soil Profile:
      LayerDepth (m)SoilUnit Weight
      10 – 5Sand\(\gamma_{bulk} = 17.5\text{ kN/m}^3\)
      25 – 15Sand\(\gamma_{sat} = 18.5\text{ kN/m}^3\)
      315 – 23 (8 m thick)Clay\(\gamma_{sat} = 17\text{ kN/m}^3\)
  • Aim: Calculate the Overconsolidation Ratio (OCR) at the mid-point of the clay layer (depth \(= 15 + 8/2 = 19\text{ m}\)).

3. Core Concepts:

Effective Stress Principle: \(\sigma' = \sigma - u\), where \(\sigma'\) is effective stress, \(\sigma\) is total stress, and \(u\) is pore water pressure.

Overconsolidation Ratio (OCR):\[OCR = \dfrac{\sigma'_c}{\sigma'_0} \]where \(\sigma'_c\) is the maximum past effective stress and \(\sigma'_0\) is the present effective stress.

Standard Assumption: When the water table drops, the soil that is no longer submerged drains and its unit weight reverts to \(\gamma_{bulk}\).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Locate the point of interest: mid-point of the clay layer at \(z = 19\text{ m}\).
  2. Calculate present effective stress (\(\sigma'_0\)) using current GWT at \(5\text{ m}\).
  3. Calculate past maximum effective stress (\(\sigma'_c\)) using past GWT at \(10\text{ m}\), applying \(\gamma_{bulk} = 17.5\text{ kN/m}^3\) for the \(5\text{ m}\) to \(10\text{ m}\) zone.
  4. Compute the OCR.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Point of Interest
    Mid-point of clay layer: \(z = 15 + \dfrac{8}{2} = 19\text{ m}\)
  2. Step 2: Present Effective Stress (\(\sigma'_0\)) — GWT at 5 m\[\sigma_0 = (5 \times 17.5) + (10 \times 18.5) + (4 \times 17) = 87.5 + 185.0 + 68.0 = 340.5\text{ kPa} \]\[u_0 = (19 - 5) \times 9.81 = 14 \times 9.81 = 137.34\text{ kPa} \]\[\sigma'_0 = 340.5 - 137.34 = 203.16\text{ kPa} \]
  3. Step 3: Past Maximum Effective Stress (\(\sigma'_c\)) — Past GWT at 10 m
    Sand from \(5\text{ m}\) to \(10\text{ m}\) is drained; apply \(\gamma_{bulk} = 17.5\text{ kN/m}^3\) to entire \(0\)–\(10\text{ m}\) zone.\[\sigma_c = (10 \times 17.5) + (5 \times 18.5) + (4 \times 17) = 175.0 + 92.5 + 68.0 = 335.5\text{ kPa} \]\[u_c = (19 - 10) \times 9.81 = 9 \times 9.81 = 88.29\text{ kPa} \]\[\sigma'_c = 335.5 - 88.29 = 247.21\text{ kPa} \]
  4. Step 4: Calculate OCR\[OCR = \dfrac{\sigma'_c}{\sigma'_0} = \dfrac{247.21}{203.16} = 1.2168 \approx 1.22 \]

Note: If the \(5\)–\(10\text{ m}\) layer is assumed to remain saturated due to capillary action (\(\gamma = 18.5\text{ kN/m}^3\)), then \(\sigma'_c = 252.21\text{ kPa}\) and \(OCR = 1.24\). The official GATE answer range (1.18–1.26) accommodates both interpretations; reverting to bulk unit weight is the most standard approach.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1.22  |  Accepted key range: 1.18 to 1.26

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q45
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A retaining wall of height 10 m with clay backfill is shown in the figure (not to scale). Weight of the retaining wall is 5000 kN per m acting at 3.3 m from the toe of the retaining wall. The interface friction angle between base of the retaining wall and the base soil is 20°. The depth of clay in front of the retaining wall is 2.0 m. The properties of the clay backfill and the clay placed in front of the retaining wall are the same. Assume that the tension crack is filled with water. Use Rankine’s earth pressure theory. Take unit weight of water, γw = 9.81 kN/m³.



The factor of safety (round off to two decimal places) against sliding failure of the retaining wall after ignoring the passive earth pressure will be ___________
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Earth Pressure & Retaining Walls

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Wall height, \(H = 10\text{ m}\)
    • Weight of wall, \(W = 5000\text{ kN/m}\)
    • Base interface friction angle, \(\delta = 20^\circ\)
    • Clay backfill: \(\gamma = 17.2\text{ kN/m}^3\), \(\phi = 0^\circ\), \(c = 30\text{ kN/m}^2\)
    • Tension crack filled with water (\(\gamma_w = 9.81\text{ kN/m}^3\))
    • Passive earth pressure is ignored.
  • Aim: Find the Factor of Safety (FOS) against sliding failure.

3. Core Concepts:

Rankine's Active Earth Pressure (Cohesive Soil): For \(\phi = 0^\circ\), \(K_a = 1\).
Active pressure at depth \(z\): \(p_a = \gamma z - 2c\)

Depth of Tension Crack (\(z_c\)): Depth where active pressure = 0.\[z_c = \dfrac{2c}{\gamma\sqrt{K_a}} = \dfrac{2c}{\gamma} \]

Hydrostatic Force in Tension Crack (\(P_w\)): Water in the tension crack exerts an outward lateral hydrostatic force.

Factor of Safety against Sliding:\[FOS = \dfrac{\text{Resisting Forces } (F_R)}{\text{Driving Forces } (F_D)} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine the depth of the tension crack \(z_c\).
  2. Calculate the active earth thrust \(P_a\) (acting from \(z_c\) to \(H\)).
  3. Calculate the water thrust \(P_w\) from the tension crack.
  4. Total driving force \(F_D = P_a + P_w\).
  5. Resisting force \(F_R = W\tan(\delta)\). (Note: Base width \(B\) and adhesion factor are not provided, so base adhesion is not added.)
  6. Compute \(FOS = F_R / F_D\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Depth of Tension Crack (\(z_c\))\[z_c = \dfrac{2c}{\gamma} = \dfrac{2 \times 30}{17.2} = 3.4884\text{ m} \]
  2. Step 2: Active Earth Thrust (\(P_a\))
    Pressure at the base (\(z = 10\text{ m}\)):\[p_{a,base} = \gamma H - 2c = (17.2 \times 10) - (2 \times 30) = 172 - 60 = 112\text{ kN/m}^2 \]The pressure distribution is triangular from 0 at \(z_c\) to \(112\text{ kN/m}^2\) at \(H\):\[P_a = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 112 \times (10 - 3.4884) = 56 \times 6.5116 = 364.65\text{ kN/m} \]
  3. Step 3: Water Thrust in Tension Crack (\(P_w\))\[P_w = \dfrac{1}{2}\gamma_w z_c^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 9.81 \times (3.4884)^2 = 59.69\text{ kN/m} \]
  4. Step 4: Total Driving Force (\(F_D\))\[F_D = P_a + P_w = 364.65 + 59.69 = 424.34\text{ kN/m} \]
  5. Step 5: Resisting Force (\(F_R\))\[F_R = W\tan\delta = 5000 \times \tan(20^\circ) = 5000 \times 0.36397 = 1819.85\text{ kN/m} \]
  6. Step 6: Factor of Safety\[FOS = \dfrac{F_R}{F_D} = \dfrac{1819.85}{424.34} = 4.29 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 4.29  |  Accepted key range: 4.20 to 4.35

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q46
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A combined trapezoidal footing of length L supports two identical square columns (P₁ and P₂) of size 0.5 m × 0.5 m, as shown in the figure. The columns P₁ and P₂ carry loads of 2000 kN and 1500 kN, respectively.



If the stress beneath the footing is uniform, the length of the combined footing L (in m, round off to two decimal places) is ___________
questions.explanation:
Structural Engineering | Shallow Foundations (Combined Footing)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Trapezoidal footing length = \(L\)
    • Column loads: \(P_1 = 2000\text{ kN}\), \(P_2 = 1500\text{ kN}\) (both \(0.5\text{ m} \times 0.5\text{ m}\))
    • Center-to-center distance between columns = \(5\text{ m}\)
    • Left edge width, \(a = 5\text{ m}\); Right edge width, \(b = 1.5\text{ m}\)
  • Aim: Determine the length \(L\) such that the soil bearing stress beneath the footing is strictly uniform.

3. Core Concepts:

Condition for Uniform Pressure: The resultant of all applied vertical column loads must coincide with the geometric centroid of the footing area.

Centroid of a Trapezoid (distance \(\bar{x}_{area}\) from the base of width \(a\)):\[\bar{x}_{area} = \dfrac{L}{3}\left(\dfrac{2b + a}{a + b}\right) \]where \(L\) is the length (height) of the trapezoid.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Place the reference origin at the extreme left edge of the footing.
  2. Locate column \(P_1\): center at \(x_1 = 0.5/2 = 0.25\text{ m}\) from the left edge.
  3. Locate column \(P_2\): center at \(x_2 = 0.25 + 5 = 5.25\text{ m}\) from the left edge.
  4. Find the Center of Gravity of loads (\(\bar{x}_{load}\)).
  5. Equate \(\bar{x}_{load}\) to \(\bar{x}_{area}\) and solve for \(L\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Position of Resultant Load (\(\bar{x}_{load}\))
    Taking moments about the extreme left edge:\[\bar{x}_{load} = \dfrac{P_1 x_1 + P_2 x_2}{P_1 + P_2} = \dfrac{2000(0.25) + 1500(5.25)}{2000 + 1500} = \dfrac{500 + 7875}{3500} = \dfrac{8375}{3500} = 2.3928\text{ m} \]
  2. Step 2: Area Centroid of Trapezoid (\(\bar{x}_{area}\))
    With \(a = 5\text{ m}\) (left edge) and \(b = 1.5\text{ m}\) (right edge):\[\bar{x}_{area} = \dfrac{L}{3}\left(\dfrac{2(1.5) + 5}{5 + 1.5}\right) = \dfrac{L}{3}\left(\dfrac{8}{6.5}\right) = \dfrac{8L}{19.5} \]
  3. Step 3: Equate and Solve for \(L\)\[\bar{x}_{load} = \bar{x}_{area} \]\[2.3928 = \dfrac{8L}{19.5} \]\[L = 2.3928 \times \dfrac{19.5}{8} = 5.8325\text{ m} \approx 5.83\text{ m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 5.83 m  |  Accepted key range: 5.70 to 5.90

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q47
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
An unsupported slope of height 15 m is shown in the figure (not to scale), in which the slope face makes an angle 50° with the horizontal. The slope material comprises purely cohesive soil having undrained cohesion 75 kPa. A trial slip circle KLM, with a radius 25 m, passes through the crest and toe of the slope and it subtends an angle 60° at its center O. The weight of the active soil mass (W, bounded by KLMN) is 2500 kN/m, which is acting at a horizontal distance of 10 m from the toe of the slope. Consider the water table to be present at a very large depth from the ground surface.



Considering the trial slip circle KLM, the factor of safety against the failure of slope under undrained condition (round off to two decimal places) is ___________
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Stability of Slopes

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Slope height \(H = 15\text{ m}\)
    • Undrained cohesion \(c_u = 75\text{ kPa}\), purely cohesive (\(\phi_u = 0^\circ\))
    • Radius of slip circle \(R = 25\text{ m}\)
    • Angle subtended by slip circle at center O, \(\theta = 60^\circ\)
    • Weight of active soil mass \(W = 2500\text{ kN/m}\)
    • Horizontal distance of \(W\) from the toe \(= 10\text{ m}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the Factor of Safety (FOS) against slope failure under undrained conditions.

3. Core Concepts:

Swedish Circle Method (Undrained Analysis): For purely cohesive soil (\(\phi = 0\)), the resisting moment is derived purely from cohesion acting along the arc length of the slip circle.\[M_R = c_u \cdot L \cdot R \]where \(L = R \cdot \theta_{rad}\) is the arc length.

Actuating (Driving) Moment:\[M_A = W \cdot \bar{x} \]where \(\bar{x}\) is the horizontal distance from the center of rotation O to the line of action of \(W\).

Factor of Safety:\[FOS = \dfrac{M_R}{M_A} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Interpretation: The driving moment \(M_A\) requires the horizontal distance of \(W\) from center O. Based on the diagram, O lies vertically above the toe K, so the lever arm equals the given horizontal distance from the toe: \(\bar{x} = 10\text{ m}\).
    (Note: If O is strictly above the toe, the vertical drop \(R - R\cos(60^\circ) = 12.5\text{ m}\) technically differs from the stated height of 15 m. In such GATE ambiguities, the explicitly labelled moment arm parameter (10 m) takes precedence.)
  2. Calculate arc length \(L\).
  3. Calculate Resisting Moment \(M_R\) and Actuating Moment \(M_A\).
  4. Divide \(M_R\) by \(M_A\) to obtain FOS.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Arc Length Calculation\[\theta_{rad} = 60^\circ \times \dfrac{\pi}{180^\circ} = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians} \]\[L = R \cdot \theta_{rad} = 25 \times \dfrac{\pi}{3} = 26.1799\text{ m} \]
  2. Step 2: Resisting Moment (\(M_R\))\[M_R = c_u \cdot L \cdot R = 75 \times 26.1799 \times 25 = 49{,}087.39\text{ kN·m/m} \]
  3. Step 3: Actuating Moment (\(M_A\))\[M_A = W \cdot \bar{x} = 2500 \times 10 = 25{,}000\text{ kN·m/m} \]
  4. Step 4: Factor of Safety\[FOS = \dfrac{M_R}{M_A} = \dfrac{49{,}087.39}{25{,}000} = 1.963 \approx 1.96 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1.96  |  Accepted key range: 1.94 to 1.98

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q48
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: An unlined canal under regime conditions along with a silt factor of 1 has a width of flow 71.25 m. Assuming the unlined canal as a wide channel, the corresponding average depth of flow (in m, round off to two decimal places) in the canal will be ___________
questions.explanation:
Water Resources Engineering | Open Channel Flow (Regime Theory)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Unlined canal in regime condition
    • Silt factor \(f = 1\)
    • Width of flow \(B = 71.25\text{ m}\)
    • Channel assumed "wide": Hydraulic Radius \(R \approx\) depth \(y\), Wetted Perimeter \(P \approx B\)
  • Aim: Find the average depth of flow \(y\) (in m).

3. Core Concepts:

Lacey's Regime Theory:

  • Wetted Perimeter: \(P = 4.75\sqrt{Q}\)
  • Flow Velocity: \(V = \left(\dfrac{Qf^2}{140}\right)^{1/6}\)
  • Hydraulic Radius: \(R = \dfrac{5}{2}\dfrac{V^2}{f}\)

Wide Channel Assumption: \(P \approx B\) and \(R \approx y\).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Equate \(P\) to \(B\) to find regime discharge \(Q\).
  2. Use Lacey's velocity equation to find mean velocity \(V\).
  3. Calculate depth using \(y = Q/(B \cdot V)\) or Lacey's hydraulic radius relation \(y \approx R = 2.5V^2/f\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Calculate Discharge (\(Q\))\[P = 4.75\sqrt{Q} \implies 71.25 = 4.75\sqrt{Q} \]\[\sqrt{Q} = \dfrac{71.25}{4.75} = 15 \implies Q = 225\text{ m}^3\text{/s} \]
  2. Step 2: Calculate Velocity (\(V\))\[V = \left(\dfrac{225 \times 1^2}{140}\right)^{1/6} = (1.6071)^{1/6} = 1.082\text{ m/s} \]
  3. Step 3: Calculate Depth (\(y\))
    Method A (Using Area):\[A = \dfrac{Q}{V} = \dfrac{225}{1.082} = 207.95\text{ m}^2 \implies y = \dfrac{A}{B} = \dfrac{207.95}{71.25} = 2.918\text{ m} \]Method B (Using Hydraulic Radius):\[y \approx R = \dfrac{5}{2}\dfrac{V^2}{f} = 2.5 \times \dfrac{(1.082)^2}{1} = 2.5 \times 1.1707 = 2.926\text{ m} \]Both methods yield \(y \approx 2.92\text{ m}\).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 2.92 m  |  Accepted key range: 2.80 to 2.95

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q49
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question:
A cylinder (2.0 m diameter, 3.0 m long and 25 kN weight) is acted upon by water on one side and oil (specific gravity = 0.8) on other side as shown in the figure.



The absolute ratio of the net magnitude of vertical forces to the net magnitude of horizontal forces (round off to two decimal places) is ___________
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Hydrostatic Forces on Curved Surfaces

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Cylinder: Diameter \(D = 2.0\text{ m}\) (Radius \(R = 1.0\text{ m}\)), Length \(L = 3.0\text{ m}\)
    • Cylinder weight \(W = 25\text{ kN}\)
    • Left fluid: Water (\(\gamma_w = 9.81\text{ kN/m}^3\)), free surface \(1.0\text{ m}\) above top of cylinder
    • Right fluid: Oil (SG \(= 0.8 \Rightarrow \gamma_{oil} = 7.848\text{ kN/m}^3\)), free surface at the cylinder's horizontal centerline (oil depth = 1 m from bottom)
  • Aim: Absolute ratio of net vertical forces to net horizontal forces \(\left(|F_{V,net}| / |F_{H,net}|\right)\).

3. Core Concepts:

Horizontal Hydrostatic Force (\(F_H\)): Equals the force on the projected vertical plane.\[F_H = \gamma \cdot \bar{h} \cdot A_{proj} \]

Vertical Hydrostatic Force (\(F_V\)): By Archimedes' principle, the upward vertical force equals the weight of fluid displaced by the relevant volume of the body up to the free surface.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate \(F_H\) from left (water) and right (oil); find \(F_{H,net}\).
  2. Calculate upward \(F_V\) from left half (water) and bottom-right quarter (oil).
  3. Subtract cylinder weight to find \(F_{V,net}\).
  4. Compute the ratio.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Net Horizontal Force (\(F_{H,net}\))
    Left (Water): Full vertical projection \(A_{proj} = 2 \times 3 = 6\text{ m}^2\); centroid depth \(\bar{h}_w = 1 + 1 = 2\text{ m}\).\[F_{H,w} = 9.81 \times 2 \times 6 = 117.72\text{ kN} \rightarrow (\text{rightward}) \]Right (Oil): Bottom half projection \(A_{proj} = 1 \times 3 = 3\text{ m}^2\); centroid depth \(\bar{h}_o = 0.5\text{ m}\).\[F_{H,o} = 7.848 \times 0.5 \times 3 = 11.772\text{ kN} \leftarrow (\text{leftward}) \]\[F_{H,net} = 117.72 - 11.772 = 105.948\text{ kN} \]
  2. Step 2: Net Vertical Fluid Force (\(F_{V,fluid}\))
    Left (Water) — upward force on left semi-cylinder:\[V_{left} = \dfrac{1}{2}\pi(1)^2 \times 3 = 1.5\pi\text{ m}^3 \]\[F_{V,w} = 1.5\pi \times 9.81 = 46.228\text{ kN} \uparrow \]Right (Oil) — upward force on bottom-right quarter cylinder:\[V_{right} = \dfrac{1}{4}\pi(1)^2 \times 3 = 0.75\pi\text{ m}^3 \]\[F_{V,o} = 0.75\pi \times 7.848 = 18.491\text{ kN} \uparrow \]\[F_{V,fluid} = 46.228 + 18.491 = 64.719\text{ kN} \uparrow \]
  3. Step 3: Net Vertical Force Including Weight\[F_{V,net} = F_{V,fluid} - W = 64.719 - 25 = 39.719\text{ kN} \uparrow \]
  4. Step 4: Absolute Ratio\[\text{Ratio} = \dfrac{|F_{V,net}|}{|F_{H,net}|} = \dfrac{39.719}{105.948} = 0.3748 \approx 0.37 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.37  |  Accepted key range: 0.35 to 0.40

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q50
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: A tube-well of 20 cm diameter fully penetrates a horizontal, homogeneous and isotropic confined aquifer of infinite horizontal extent. The aquifer is of 30 m uniform thickness. A steady pumping at the rate of 40 litres/s from the well for a long time results in a steady drawdown of 4 m at the well face. The subsurface flow to the well due to pumping is steady, horizontal and Darcian and the radius of influence of the well is 245 m. The hydraulic conductivity of the aquifer (in m/day, round off to integer) is ___________
questions.explanation:
Hydrology | Well Hydraulics

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Tube-well diameter \(= 20\text{ cm} \Rightarrow r_w = 0.1\text{ m}\)
    • Aquifer thickness \(B = 30\text{ m}\)
    • Discharge \(Q = 40\text{ L/s}\)
    • Drawdown at well face \(s_w = 4\text{ m}\)
    • Radius of influence \(R = 245\text{ m}\)
  • Aim: Calculate Hydraulic conductivity \(K\) in m/day.

3. Core Concepts:

Thiem's Equation for Confined Aquifer:\[Q = \dfrac{2\pi K B s_w}{\ln(R/r_w)} \]where \(Q\) must be in m³/day to yield \(K\) in m/day.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Convert \(Q\) from L/s to m³/day.
  2. Substitute all variables into Thiem's equation.
  3. Solve for \(K\) and round to the nearest integer.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Unit Conversions\[Q = 40\text{ L/s} = 0.04\text{ m}^3\text{/s} \]\[Q = 0.04 \times 3600 \times 24 = 3456\text{ m}^3\text{/day} \]\[r_w = 10\text{ cm} = 0.1\text{ m} \]
  2. Step 2: Evaluate Thiem's Equation\[3456 = \dfrac{2\pi \cdot K \cdot 30 \cdot 4}{\ln(245/0.1)} = \dfrac{240\pi \cdot K}{\ln(2450)} \]\[\ln(2450) \approx 7.8038 \]
  3. Step 3: Solve for \(K\)\[K = \dfrac{3456 \times 7.8038}{240\pi} = \dfrac{26{,}969.93}{753.98} = 35.77\text{ m/day} \approx 36\text{ m/day} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 36 m/day  |  Accepted key range: 34 to 38

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q51
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: A baghouse filter has to treat 12 m³/s of waste gas continuously. The baghouse is to be divided into 5 sections of equal cloth area such that one section can be shut down for cleaning and/or repairing, while the other 4 sections continue to operate. An air-to-cloth ratio of 6.0 m³/min-m² cloth will provide sufficient treatment to the gas. The individual bags are of 32 cm in diameter and 5 m in length. The total number of bags (in integer) required in the baghouse is ___________
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Air Pollution Control

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Total waste gas flow \(Q = 12\text{ m}^3\text{/s}\)
    • Baghouse structure: 5 equal sections (4 active, 1 offline for cleaning)
    • Air-to-cloth ratio \(V = 6.0\text{ m}^3/\text{min·m}^2 = 6.0\text{ m/min}\)
    • Bag dimensions: Diameter \(D = 32\text{ cm} = 0.32\text{ m}\), Length \(L = 5\text{ m}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the total number of bags required in the baghouse.

3. Core Concepts:

Filtration Area Required: Determined by the flow rate and allowable air-to-cloth ratio during the most demanding state (1 section offline).\[A_{active} = \dfrac{Q_{total}}{V} \]

Surface Area of One Bag (ends not counted in active cloth area):\[A_{bag} = \pi \cdot D \cdot L \]

Total Bags: Must be equally distributed among all 5 sections.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Convert total flow rate \(Q\) to m³/min.
  2. Calculate active cloth area required for 4 functioning sections.
  3. Determine cloth area required per section.
  4. Calculate total cloth area installed across all 5 sections.
  5. Find number of bags per section (rounding up) and multiply by 5.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Convert Flow Rate\[Q_{total} = 12\text{ m}^3\text{/s} \times 60\text{ s/min} = 720\text{ m}^3\text{/min} \]
  2. Step 2: Active Cloth Area Required\[A_{active} = \dfrac{720}{6.0} = 120\text{ m}^2 \](served by the 4 online sections)
  3. Step 3: Area Per Section and Total Installed Area\[A_{\text{per section}} = \dfrac{120}{4} = 30\text{ m}^2 \]\[A_{\text{total installed}} = 30 \times 5 = 150\text{ m}^2 \]
  4. Step 4: Surface Area of One Bag\[A_{bag} = \pi \times 0.32 \times 5 = 1.6\pi \approx 5.0265\text{ m}^2 \]
  5. Step 5: Number of Bags\[\text{Bags per section} = \dfrac{30}{5.0265} = 5.968 \rightarrow \text{round up to } 6 \]\[\text{Total bags} = 6 \times 5 = 30\text{ bags} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 30 bags  |  Accepted key range: 30 to 30

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q52
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: A secondary clarifier handles a total flow of 9600 m³/d from the aeration tank of a conventional activated-sludge treatment system. The concentration of solids in the flow from the aeration tank is 3000 mg/L. The clarifier is required to thicken the solids to 12000 mg/L, and hence it is to be designed for a solid flux of \( 3.2 \dfrac{\text{kg}}{\text{m}^2 \cdot \text{h}} \). The surface area of the designed clarifier for thickening (in m², in integer) is ___________
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Wastewater Treatment / Secondary Clarifier

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Total flow from aeration tank, \(Q = 9600\text{ m}^3\text{/d}\)
    • Concentration of solids (MLSS), \(X_0 = 3000\text{ mg/L}\)
    • Target thickened solids concentration, \(X_u = 12000\text{ mg/L}\)
    • Limiting solid flux, \(SF = 3.2\text{ kg/(m}^2\text{·h)}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the surface area (\(A\)) of the designed clarifier required for thickening in m².

3. Core Concepts:

Solid Mass Balance: The total mass of solids applied to the clarifier per day (\(M_s\)) is the product of incoming flow rate and incoming solids concentration.\[M_s = Q \times X_0 \]

Area Requirement:\[A = \dfrac{M_s}{SF} \]

Note: The target thickened concentration (\(X_u\)) is a distractor for the area calculation via solid flux method. It would be used if calculating the underflow rate \(Q_u = \dfrac{QX_0}{X_u}\).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Convert flow and concentration into compatible mass flow units (kg/d).
  2. Convert limiting solid flux from kg/(m²·h) to kg/(m²·d).
  3. Divide total solids mass by the converted solid flux to obtain surface area.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Total Mass of Solids Applied (\(M_s\))\[X_0 = 3000\text{ mg/L} = 3000\text{ g/m}^3 = 3\text{ kg/m}^3 \]\[M_s = 9600\text{ m}^3\text{/d} \times 3\text{ kg/m}^3 = 28{,}800\text{ kg/d} \]
  2. Step 2: Convert Limiting Solid Flux to Daily Basis\[SF = 3.2\text{ kg/(m}^2\text{·h)} \times 24\text{ h/d} = 76.8\text{ kg/(m}^2\text{·d)} \]
  3. Step 3: Required Surface Area\[A = \dfrac{M_s}{SF} = \dfrac{28{,}800}{76.8} = 375\text{ m}^2 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 375 m²  |  Accepted key range: 375 to 375

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q53
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question: Spot speeds of vehicles observed at a point on a highway are 40, 55, 60, 65 and 80 km/h. The space-mean speed (in km/h, round off to two decimal places) of the observed vehicles is ___________
questions.explanation:
Transportation Engineering | Traffic Engineering / Speed Studies

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Application
  • Given Data: Spot speeds of \(n = 5\) observed vehicles: \(v_1 = 40\), \(v_2 = 55\), \(v_3 = 60\), \(v_4 = 65\), \(v_5 = 80\text{ km/h}\).
  • Aim: Calculate the space-mean speed in km/h (rounded to two decimal places).

3. Core Concepts:

Space-Mean Speed (\(V_s\)): The harmonic mean of the spot speeds; represents the average speed based on the average time taken to cover a unit distance.\[V_s = \dfrac{n}{\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{n} \dfrac{1}{v_i}} \]

Common Pitfall: Do not confuse with Time-Mean Speed (\(V_t\)), which is the simple arithmetic mean: \(V_t = \dfrac{\sum v_i}{n}\).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate the reciprocal of each observed speed.
  2. Sum these reciprocals.
  3. Divide the total number of observations (\(n\)) by this sum.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Sum of Reciprocals
    Speed (km/h)Reciprocal (h/km)
    400.025000
    550.018182
    600.016667
    650.015385
    800.012500
    Sum0.087734
  2. Step 2: Space-Mean Speed\[V_s = \dfrac{5}{0.087734} = 56.9904\ldots\text{ km/h} \approx 56.99\text{ km/h} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 56.99 km/h  |  Accepted key range: 55.50 to 58.50

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q54
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question:
The longitudinal section of a runway provides the following data:

End-to-end runway (m)Gradient (%)
0 to 300+ 1.2
300 to 600– 0.7
600 to 1100+ 0.6
1100 to 1400– 0.8
1400 to 1700– 1.0

The effective gradient of the runway (in %, round off to two decimal places) is ___________
questions.explanation:
Transportation Engineering | Airport Engineering / Runway Geometric Design

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension / Application
  • Given Data:
    Chainage (m)Gradient
    0 to 300+1.2%
    300 to 600−0.7%
    600 to 1100+0.6%
    1100 to 1400−0.8%
    1400 to 1700−1.0%
  • Aim: Determine the effective gradient of the runway in %.

3. Core Concepts:

Effective Runway Gradient (ICAO): The maximum difference in elevation between the highest and lowest points on the longitudinal profile, divided by the total runway length.\[\text{Effective Gradient (\%)} = \left(\dfrac{E_{max} - E_{min}}{\text{Total Length}}\right) \times 100 \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Assume an arbitrary RL at chainage 0 (e.g., 0.00 m).
  2. Calculate elevation at each gradient change by accumulating rise and fall.
  3. Identify the absolute highest and lowest elevations.
  4. Apply the effective gradient formula.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Elevations at Each Chainage Point (assuming RL = 0.00 m at chainage 0)
    Chainage (m)CalculationElevation (m)
    0—0.00
    300\(0.00 + 300 \times \dfrac{1.2}{100}\)+3.60
    600\(3.60 + 300 \times \dfrac{-0.7}{100}\)+1.50
    1100\(1.50 + 500 \times \dfrac{0.6}{100}\)+4.50
    1400\(4.50 + 300 \times \dfrac{-0.8}{100}\)+2.10
    1700\(2.10 + 300 \times \dfrac{-1.0}{100}\)−0.90
  2. Step 2: Identify Maximum and Minimum Elevations
    • \(E_{max} = +4.50\text{ m}\) (at chainage 1100 m)
    • \(E_{min} = -0.90\text{ m}\) (at chainage 1700 m)
    • Maximum difference \(= 4.50 - (-0.90) = 5.40\text{ m}\)
  3. Step 3: Effective Gradient\[\text{Effective Gradient} = \left(\dfrac{5.40}{1700}\right) \times 100 = 0.3176\% \approx 0.32\% \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.32%  |  Accepted key range: 0.30 to 0.34

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q55
questions.subject: Surveying & Geomatics
questions.question: Traversing is carried out for a closed traverse PQRS. The internal angles at vertices P, Q, R and S are measured as 92°, 68°, 123°, and 77°, respectively. If fore bearing of line PQ is 27°, fore bearing of line RS (in degrees, in integer) is ___________
questions.explanation:
Geomatics / Surveying | Traverse Surveying / Bearings and Angles

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Closed traverse PQRS (4 sides)
    • Internal angles: \(\angle P = 92^\circ\), \(\angle Q = 68^\circ\), \(\angle R = 123^\circ\), \(\angle S = 77^\circ\)
    • Fore bearing (FB) of line PQ \(= 27^\circ\)
  • Aim: Find the Fore bearing of line RS in degrees.

3. Core Concepts:

Sum of Internal Angles: For a polygon with \(n\) sides: \((2n-4) \times 90^\circ\). For \(n=4\): \(360^\circ\).
Sanity check: \(92^\circ + 68^\circ + 123^\circ + 77^\circ = 360^\circ\) ✓

Back Bearing: \(\text{BB} = \text{FB} \pm 180^\circ\)

Traverse Direction Ambiguity: The problem does not specify clockwise or counter-clockwise direction, leading to two valid geometric interpretations.

  • Case 1 (Counter-Clockwise): \(\text{FB of Next Line} = \text{BB of Previous Line} + \text{Internal Angle}\)
  • Case 2 (Clockwise): \(\text{FB of Next Line} = \text{BB of Previous Line} - \text{Internal Angle}\)

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

Case 1: Counter-Clockwise Traverse

  1. \(\text{FB}_{PQ} = 27^\circ \Rightarrow \text{BB}_{PQ} = 27^\circ + 180^\circ = 207^\circ\)
  2. \(\text{FB}_{QR} = 207^\circ + 68^\circ = 275^\circ \Rightarrow \text{BB}_{QR} = 275^\circ - 180^\circ = 95^\circ\)
  3. \(\text{FB}_{RS} = 95^\circ + 123^\circ = \mathbf{218^\circ}\)

Closure verification: \(\text{BB}_{RS} = 38^\circ \Rightarrow \text{FB}_{SP} = 115^\circ \Rightarrow \text{BB}_{SP} = 295^\circ \Rightarrow \text{FB}_{PQ} = 295^\circ + 92^\circ = 387^\circ - 360^\circ = 27^\circ\) ✓


Case 2: Clockwise Traverse

  1. \(\text{FB}_{PQ} = 27^\circ \Rightarrow \text{BB}_{PQ} = 207^\circ\)
